tob-0161: In this early Jung work, the great Swiss thinker breaks with Freud and maps the unconscious as a sea of mythic images. He reads a patient’s fantasies as the mind speaking in the tongue of old legend. Beatrice Hinkle’s translation brought Jung to America — and sowed the seeds of his later teaching on archetypes.
tob-10261: Athanasius Kircher’s Great Art of Light and Shadow — 1646 — is the Jesuit polymath’s vast illustrated treatise on optics. Sundials, lenses, projection, and the magic lantern all find their place. His baroque curiosity embraced the whole of nature. The work is a monument of seventeenth-century science.
tob-10361: Johann Wier’s Pseudomonarchia Daemonum — 1563 — catalogs the sixty-nine demons of hell, with their ranks, seals, and offices. The physician’s list became the source for the Goetia’s seventy-two spirits. His work founded the literature of demonology. It remains essential for students of the grimoires.
cia-0000102961: A July 1987 report on Moscow's work-treatment camps, Soviet institutions where alcoholics and drug users were confined and put to work as a supposed cure. The awkward official name covered a system of forced labor aimed at social problems the state wanted to hide. This document shows American intelligence tracking the harsher edges of Soviet social policy.
cia-0000105161: A weekly terrorism briefing dated January 2, 1975, summing up attacks and threats around the world for American officials. These regular reports tracked bombings, hijackings, and assassinations as political violence rose in the 1970s. Reading it now is a reminder of how early the modern age of international terrorism began.
cia-0000109061: An October 1967 report on Cuban sugar production in 1967 and the outlook for 1968 and 1970. Sugar was Cuba's lifeblood and the measure of Castro's grand harvest campaigns. The CIA tracked the cane harvest like a stock price — because in Cuba, sugar tonnage was politics.
cia-0000119761: A chronology special supplement from September 1956 — extra timeline material on the Hungarian crisis. Supplements gathered the details too fine for the main narrative. The entry is history's footnotes, filed while the history was still being written.
cia-0000126861: A February 1953 file on John P. Hayes — a name without a story in the catalog record. Thousands of such name files fill the archive: persons of interest, contacts, or simply names that crossed a report. The entry is a placeholder for a history the full text may hold.
cia-0000126961: An October 1968 study titled Haiti: Duvalier's Primitive Totalitarian State. Papa Doc ruled through voodoo mystique, secret police, and terror — totalitarianism on a shoestring. The document dissects one of history's strangest dictatorships with clinical care.
cia-0000132661: A 1960 forecast titled Prospects for the Castro Regime. Analysts were asking the essential question: would the revolution survive? The document is the odds, calculated: the regime's future, weighed.
cia-0000135861: A 1952 routing and record sheet with an attached memo titled Guatemala — the archive's punctuation garbles the quotes. The bureaucracy of covert action: forms, routing slips, memos. The entry is the paperwork: the operation, administered.
cia-0000136061: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on the K Program. The program, referenced. The document is the file: the K Program, noted — the details, elsewhere.
cia-0000136161: A 1954 cable to LINCOLN with headquarters' criticisms and recommendations. Washington graded the field's work. The document is the review: the criticism, delivered — the recommendations, attached.
cia-0000136261: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN requesting waiting until June 20 for a decision before taking action — the truncated title cuts off what. The pause, requested. The document is the delay: the decision, awaited.
cia-0000136961: A 1954 cable requesting an appropriate man send letters to Salem delegates and non-something — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The letter campaign. The document is the request: the letters, sent.
cia-0000139161: An estimated 1985 document on the distribution of particularly sensitive intelligence — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The most secret reports, routed. The document is the distribution: the sensitivity, handled.
un-ga-res-a-69-61: General Assembly Resolution A/69/61, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The Assembly's numbered business. The designation and year align; the decision lives in the text.
un-ga-res-57-161: General Assembly Resolution 57/161, adopted in 2004 during the 57th session — this one is off by two years, a small puzzle. The designation is preserved; the date is questioned.
un-ga-res-161: Resolution 161 of the General Assembly, adopted in 1961. The Congo crisis year's Assembly. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-161: Security Council Resolution 161, adopted in February 1961 — the Congo resolution authorizing the UN force to use all necessary measures to prevent civil war, passed days after Patrice Lumumba's murder. The peacekeepers became enforcers. The resolution is the escalation: the mandate, hardened.
un-sc-res-661: Security Council Resolution 661, adopted in August 1990 — the Iraq sanctions resolution, imposing comprehensive economic sanctions days after Saddam Hussein's invasion of Kuwait. The Council's economic siege of Baghdad began here. The resolution is the siege: the economy, strangled.
un-sc-res-1461: Security Council Resolution 1461, cataloged with the year 1973 — the numbering belongs to 2003, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1661: Security Council Resolution 1661, adopted in 2006 — aligned. The deliberations continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1761: Security Council Resolution 1761, adopted in 2007 — aligned. The Council deciding. The number and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-2361: Security Council Resolution 2361, adopted in 2017 — aligned. The Council deciding. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
cia-0000132761: A 1960 CIA file titled Cuba, numbered 0000132761. The revolution's second year, documented. The document is the documentation: the island, recorded.
plos-pone-0000061: A 2006 PLOS ONE study: self-correcting maps of molecular pathways. Biological roadmaps that fix their own errors. The paper is the map: the pathways, self-repairing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d61: The ambassador in the Soviet Union, Harriman, to the president, October 26 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 61. Moscow's embassy reported. The cable is the embassy's: Harriman, informing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d161: The Secretary of State to the President and the Acting Secretary of State — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 161, closing the batch. The secretary wrote both. The memo is the close: the batch, complete.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d261: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 261. The connective thread. The note is the thread: the narrative, sewn.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d361: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, November 28, 1943 — Document 361. The Allied planners, minuted. The minutes are the combined: the chiefs, Allied.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d461: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, December 7, 1943 — Document 461, closing the batch. Pearl Harbor's second anniversary, the planners met. The minutes are the close: the batch, complete.
military-reminiscences-of-the-civil-war-: General Cox opens his Civil War reminiscences with the war's first years — from Bull Run through the western campaigns to November 1863. His clear, honest narrative ranks among the best Union memoirs ever written. Essential reading for students of the conflict.
arxiv-2605-09061: Electricity imbalance prices — what it costs to be wrong about supply and demand — swing wildly yet follow strict market rules. Runyao Yu, Julia Lin, Derek W. Bunn, and colleagues build a neural network informed by those rules to forecast the prices efficiently. The 2026 paper is energy economics with market structure baked in.
arxiv-2605-09161: Prikry forcing is a set-theoretic technique for changing the universe's combinatorics while preserving large cardinals. Tom Benhamou, Sebastiano Thei, and Ben-Zion Weltsch study the intermediate models of the strongly compact version. The 2026 paper is pure set theory on forcing and its stages.
arxiv-2605-09461: Finding software vulnerabilities with LLMs works better when the model sees the code from three angles at once. Wenxin Tang, Xiang Zhang, Junliang Liu, and colleagues augment context along triple paths for vulnerability detection — VulTriage. The 2026 paper triages security bugs like an emergency room.
arxiv-2605-09661: Meta-analyses pool dozens of medical studies into one conclusion — careful, tedious work. Huy Hoang Ha, Benoit Favre, and François Portet benchmark LLMs at synthesizing those conclusions with MedMeta. The 2026 paper tests whether AI can do evidence-based medicine's hardest synthesis.
plos-pone-0003461: Psychologists found a blink-speed clue to cocaine's brain effects in this 2008 study. Recreational cocaine users blinked less often, a sign of sluggish dopamine activity tied to fewer D2 receptors in the brain's control center. Since blink rate tracks dopamine function, the work offers a simple window into the drug's toll on self-control.
plos-pone-0003561: Virologists mapped HIV's copying machine in fine detail in this 2008 paper. Reverse transcriptase, the enzyme that turns viral RNA into DNA, locks onto its primer-template in stable complexes, and the team charted how it grips the downstream template strand. The structural details expose vulnerabilities in the enzyme every HIV drug aims to jam.
plos-pone-0003661: In 2008, a team went hunting for cancer clues in blood. Mining pooled gene data, they searched for blood markers that could flag cancer early, when it is most curable. The haul offers leads for simple blood tests that catch tumors before symptoms appear.
plos-pone-0003761: Labalette, Nouët, and Levillayer mapped a protein's dark side in this 2008 paper. The LIM-only protein FHL2, previously tied to normal growth control, was shown to drive Ras-induced transformation through cyclin D1 and p53 pathways. The finding flips a growth regulator into a cancer accomplice.
plos-pone-0003861: In 2008, a team modeled how killer T cells take aim. Combining experiments with computation, they studied how microtubule stabilization shapes T-cell polarity during attack. The work reveals the cytoskeletal choreography behind the immune system's precision strikes.
plos-pone-0003961: In 2008, Krejci, Salazar, and Kashiwada tested six bone-disease mutations head to head. Analyzing STAT1 activation by FGFR3 mutants linked to skeletal dysplasia, they undermined a dominant-negative theory. The comparative data redirect the search for how these mutations warp growth.
plos-pone-0004061: In 2008, Xiao, Ye, and Oberhollenzer tied a gene variant to blood repair cells. SDF1 gene variation tracked with circulating SDF1-alpha levels. It also tracked the number of endothelial progenitor cells. The small variant may shape how blood vessels heal and renew.
plos-pone-0004161: In 2009, Hannes Drexler paired two drugs against stubborn leukemia cells. Salubrinal plus a proteasome inhibitor drove synergistic killing of leukemic cells fast. The combo pushed stressed cancer cells into apoptosis. The one-two punch suggests a new leukemia strategy worth testing.
plos-pone-0004261: In 2009, Ng, Chow, and Sun found blood signals for chikungunya severity. IL-1beta, IL-6, and RANTES levels marked how bad the infection turned. The immune mediators tracked disease course. The trio could guide triage during outbreaks. The markers were measured in Singapore patients.
plos-pone-0004361: In 2009, Xiang, Yang, and Che hunted tumor drugs in fish tanks. Combinatorial chemistry paired with zebrafish assays found tumor cell growth inhibitors. The fish screen flagged CDK-blocking candidates. The method speeds cancer drug discovery. The live-fish test bridges chemistry and biology.
plos-pone-0358561: PROTACs are a new class of drugs that mark disease proteins for destruction by the cell’s own garbage disposal. This paper tested a PROTAC aimed at PAK4, a protein that drives bladder cancer cell growth. The compound slowed cancer cell proliferation, marking PAK4 as a vulnerable target in a hard-to-treat cancer.
plos-pone-0358761: Measuring knee joint space with ultrasound during a valgus stress test could track arthritis — if the measurement is reliable. This study tested the relative and absolute reliability of the technique. The reliability numbers tell clinicians whether to trust the reading in practice.
plos-pone-0356761: Female genital mutilation/cutting leaves lasting harm, including to sexual health. This retrospective cross-sectional study linked sexual dysfunction after FGM/C to organ-specific genital anatomy and trauma history. The associations give clinicians evidence for counseling and care — and give advocates hard data for change.
plos-pone-0357961: Smart insoles can read your day from your feet. This study classified daily activities using WalkinSense, a wireless instrumented insole, in a semi free-living setting. The classification results show how well foot sensors alone can tell sitting from strolling from climbing stairs — no wristband or phone needed.
plos-pone-0358261: Severe underbites complicate orthodontics — the thin bone housing the lower front teeth sets the limit. This CBCT study examined mandibular incisor alveolar housing and its axis relationship in untreated skeletal Class III malocclusion. The 3D measurements show orthodontists precisely how far teeth can safely be moved.
plos-pone-0357661: Census data could flag the neighborhoods where teen depression concentrates. This paper proposed a census-based adolescent depression risk assessment method, with honest reflections on its limits. The novel approach offers public health a cheap, wide net for finding at-risk youth before crisis strikes.
plos-pone-0355961: Concrete that heals its own cracks and carries recycled waste could transform construction. This paper experimentally validated sustainable engineered cementitious composites incorporating recycled materials, backed by full life cycle assessment. The composites prove their green credentials with hard data, not just claims.
plos-pone-0356461: Women with polycystic ovary syndrome show elevated levels of CTRP-1, a fat-derived signaling protein. This case–control study established that circulating CTRP-1 runs high in PCOS. The finding adds a new piece to the metabolic puzzle of a condition affecting millions of women.
plos-pone-0356261: As forests regrow, the soil’s carbon-nitrogen-phosphorus balance shifts in predictable succession. This paper tracked those successional shifts in soil C:N:P stoichiometry and their environmental controls during forest restoration in Huize County, Yunnan. The stoichiometric story reveals how recovering forests rebuild their underground economy.
plos-pone-0355561: India’s second National Mental Health Survey will shape policy for a billion-plus people — so its quality control must be airtight. This paper laid out the survey’s quality control protocol. The rigorous protocol aims to produce mental health data the nation can genuinely trust.
plos-pone-0353661: Smooth-coated otters are vanishing from the Ganga River Basin — but where should conservation focus? This paper went beyond sightings, using ensemble modeling to identify conservation hotspots for Lutrogale perspicillata. The model-driven hotspots give planners defensible priorities for protecting one of Asia’s most charismatic mammals.
plos-pone-0356061: Crop pests destroy harvests — and AI can identify them in the field. CT-PestNet is a novel pest classification model combining cross-scale feature distillation with a vision transformer using local token interaction. The sophisticated architecture brings expert-level pest identification to any farmer with a smartphone.
plos-pone-0353861: Young adults with familial heart disease in highly consanguineous populations carry genetic clues. This paper used targeted sequencing to uncover genetic insights into familial cardiovascular disease among young adults. The findings bring precision cardiology to communities where cousin marriage concentrates rare variants.
plos-pone-0355461: Oral exams in medical education are high-stakes and often haphazard. This systematic review examined structured approaches to improving their outcomes, building an evidence-based framework. The framework gives medical schools a rigorous path from subjective interrogation to fair, valid assessment.
plos-pone-0348861: Protein families hide motif–domain patterns that alignment-aware tools can reveal. ProteoMapper is such a tool — for alignment-aware identification and quantitative analysis of contextual motif–domain patterns. The software gives protein scientists a sharper lens on the sequence features that define function.
plos-pone-0354961: Young-onset diffuse gastric cancer — striking the young with a particularly vicious form — needs molecular mapping. This paper used ReliefF-based feature selection on RNA-Seq data to uncover its molecular landscape. The selected gene features point to the drivers of a cancer that defies the usual age patterns.
europmc-pmc2799461: The C8 Health Project studied people exposed to an industrial chemical known as C8, and this 2009 paper describes how the study was built. The authors lay out the design, methods, and the tens of thousands of participants enrolled. The project became one of the largest health studies of chemical exposure ever run. This paper is the blueprint other researchers use to understand its data.
europmc-pmc2815961: Whooping cough was coming back despite vaccination, and this 2009 paper found a possible reason. The authors show that circulating Bordetella pertussis strains were producing more toxin than older strains. The shift suggests the bacteria evolved under vaccine pressure. The finding forced a rethink of pertussis vaccines and surveillance.
europmc-pmc2851561: Germs race through tight-knit crowds, and this 2010 paper models the chase. The authors study how disease moves, and can be curbed, in networks with community shape. Their math shows community walls slow the rush. The work aids vaccine plans that aim at bridge people between groups.
europmc-pmc2861661: Carnitine ferries fuel into cell power plants, and shortfalls hurt. This 2010 review surveys carnitine's role in disease, from heart to nerves to aging. The authors weigh where supplements truly help and where proof is thin. Their overview guides doctors on a much-hyped nutrient with real but narrow uses.
europmc-pmc2876761: MRSA's toll in America was worse than thought. This 2007 paper counts hospital stays and deaths from methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in the United States from 1999 to 2005. The authors' tally revealed a major killer hiding in plain sight. Their numbers drove hospital hygiene drives nationwide.
europmc-pmc2965761: A muscle-wasting disease stems from a gene that will not stay quiet. This 2010 paper shows facioscapulohumeral dystrophy springs from a half-silenced jumped gene. The authors nail the mechanism. Their finding explains the disease's cruel face-first pattern. The work points to silencing-based treatments.
europmc-pmc2984261: RNA folds need predicting software. This 2010 paper brings RNAstructure, a tool for predicting and studying RNA folds. The authors' program became an RNA lab staple. Their software spread to labs worldwide. Students learn RNA folding on its diagrams. It pairs sequence with shape in one view.
europmc-pmc3035261: Genome distances got a standard recipe. This 2010 paper lays out step-by-step rules for measuring genome-to-genome distance. The authors' recipe standardizes comparisons. Their work steadies germ taxonomy. Labs now quote distances the same way. The recipe runs on free software.
europmc-pmc3045361: Brain walls got a molecular guide. This 2011 review compares the two walls guarding the brain: blood-brain and blood-fluid barriers. The author surveys their likeness and gaps. Their overview aids drug delivery. Drugs must sneak past both gatekeepers. The guide maps each wall's weak spots.
europmc-pmc3093361: Allergy-type immunity evolved for rapid repair. This 2011 paper argues the Th2 immune arm exists to patch tissue torn by parasites. The authors reframe allergy's purpose. Their work lights up immunology. Worms, not pollen, were the original foe. The reframe explains asthma's stubbornness.
europmc-pmc6543461: Monocytes and macrophages - the immune system's cleanup crew - do far more than eat germs: they start, steer, and resolve inflammation. In autoimmune disease, these same cells turn against the body's own tissues. This sweeping review details their double role across disorders like lupus and rheumatoid arthritis, and why they are prime targets for calming friendly fire.
europmc-pmc6547561: Big DNA rearrangements - deletions, duplications, inversions - cause many diseases, but the software that finds them varies wildly in accuracy. This study stress-tested the leading structural-variation detectors on whole-genome data, scoring each on what it catches and what it misses. The head-to-head results tell researchers which tool to trust for which job.
europmc-pmc6565761: When lungs fail suddenly - acute respiratory distress syndrome - intensive-care teams need clear rules fast. This paper delivers fifteen evidence-graded recommendations plus a treatment algorithm for the early phase of ARDS in adults. Built with the GRADE method by French intensive-care experts, it standardizes care for one of the ICU's deadliest emergencies.
europmc-pmc6602461: A list of interesting genes is just the start - the question is what they do together. g:Profiler answers it: paste in gene identifiers and get back the biological processes, pathways, and functions enriched in the list. The 2019 update keeps this beloved enrichment workhorse fast, current, and free.
europmc-pmc6612361: Ovarian tumors fight immunotherapy with sneaky packages: tiny vesicles loaded with arginase-1, an enzyme that starves T cells. This study found these arginase-carrying bubbles suppress immune attack and spur tumor growth. Neutralizing the vesicles - or their cargo - could unblock immunotherapy for ovarian cancer.
europmc-pmc6650661: Thematic analysis - finding patterns in interview data - is a workhorse of qualitative research, but doing it well takes method. This paper grounds the technique in descriptive phenomenology: a philosophy-first guide to reading people's lived experience faithfully. Researchers get principles for analysis that stays true to participants' voices.
europmc-pmc6711461: Diffusion MRI traces the brain's wiring - but the images are noisy, especially when scans run fast. This paper proposes a patch-based cleanup method using singular value shrinkage under realistic noise models. The math squeezes cleaner wiring maps out of rougher, quicker scans.
europmc-pmc6719561: One gene can spawn many protein variants - proteoforms - each with its own mass and job. Top-down mass spectrometry reads whole proteins intact, and this expert guide sets best practices and benchmarks for the field. The consortium's decision tree helps labs get reliable results from finicky instruments.
europmc-pmc6754461: After a heart attack, the heart scars instead of healing - but a circular RNA may change that. This study found circFndc3b boosts cardiac repair in mice after myocardial infarction, working through the FUS/VEGF-A pathway to grow new vessels. The loop of RNA could become a heart-healing therapy.
europmc-pmc6769561: Aging stokes a low-grade inflammatory fire - 'inflammaging' - and oxidative stress fans the flames. This review connects the two to the diseases of old age, from molecular mechanisms to emerging treatments. Cooling both fires, the authors argue, could extend healthy years.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-761: Buried bomb waste had no final plan in 2007 — GAO's report says the schemes for the most dangerous buried transuranic junk were unfinished, with cost guesses still soft. The findings describe the nation's hottest garbage in limbo. The report demands a real plan before the bill comes due.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-461: The Pentagon's must-protect list needed prioritizing in 2007 — GAO's report says the effort to name and rank critical sites wanted real guidance. The findings demand a method for the madness. The report's logic is plain: you cannot guard everything, so guard smart.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-361: Hiring an army of census takers needed a plan in 2007 — GAO's report says the bureau should sharpen recruiting and train its temp field force better. The findings target the people pipeline. The report's warning: the count is only as good as the counters.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-561: Cargo in transit was slipping past the watchers in 2007 — GAO's report says weak spots in the in-bond system hampered border enforcement. The findings target the tracking gaps. The report warns that the shipment nobody watches is the shipment that matters.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-161: Reading First was working, mostly, in 2007, and GAO's report says states saw better reading instruction, though clearer federal procedures were needed. The findings balance credit and critique. The report asks whether the littlest readers were really winning. The youngest readers were counting on it.
openalex-w7207669761: Good science class is not about memorizing facts; it is about building arguments from evidence. This study looks at what happens when teachers get trained to lead classroom debate and investigation in science lessons. The authors measured how that training changed what teachers do and how students build scientific knowledge. The paper makes the case that arguing well, in the scientific sense, is a skill students can and should practice.
openalex-w7205011561: Listeria monocytogenes is a food-borne bacterium that can turn deadly, especially for pregnant women, newborns, and the elderly. This study examines how it causes disease, how it forms stubborn biofilms on food equipment, and what it means for public health. The authors pull together the science of a pathogen that thrives in refrigerators. A microbiology review with direct lessons for food safety.
openalex-w7205012761: Wet age-related macular degeneration is a leading cause of permanent vision loss in older adults. This study tracks how drug-treatment guidelines for the condition evolved in one Brazilian state between 2018 and 2025. The authors map changing indications and use of the medicines. A focused ophthalmology study that shows how fast eye care advances, and who gets access to it.
openalex-w7130562261: UTe2 is a superconductor that may pair electrons in an unusual way. This experimental paper probed its superconducting state by measuring heat capacity while rotating a magnetic field around a pristine crystal. The authors mapped how the signal varies with angle at 2.1 kelvin. A low-temperature study hunting the fingerprint of exotic pairing.
openalex-w7214129061: Air plunging down from the stratosphere can brew severe weather. This paper ran 3D models of merging high-spin air blobs, tracking their stats and shapes. The team charted the swirl dynamics. An air-science study of the sky's diving intruders and the storms they seed.
pmc-13468761: This 2026 machine learning paper introduces BiasFormer, a transformer model for temporal action segmentation — the task of labeling what action happens at each moment in a video. By guiding the model's posterior estimates in a structured way, it sharpens the boundary detection between actions. The work targets better video understanding for editing, robotics, and surveillance.
pmc-13472161: In this 2026 biophysics paper, scientists fused red blood cell membrane material into artificial liposomes — tiny fat bubbles used as drug carriers — and measured how the incorporation changed their stability and fusion behavior. Biomimetic liposomes that behave more like real cells could deliver drugs more safely. The study reports the stability trade-offs.
pmc-13434361: A 2026 surgical study examining whether the circular stapler platform used in left colectomy and high anterior resection affects the risk of anastomotic leakage — the dangerous complication where the reconnected bowel leaks. Stapler choice is a concrete, modifiable factor. The study gives surgeons data on a device-level decision.
pmc-13474961: A 2026 chemistry paper on stereoselective epimerization of 1,3-diols — flipping the 3D arrangement at specific carbons — using a chiral hydrogen-atom abstraction catalyst. Controlling stereochemistry precisely is the core challenge of organic synthesis. The new catalyst gives chemists a sharper tool.
pmc-13529361: This 2026 lung cancer study — the "Rebiopsy on Osi" study — examined EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer progressing on first-line osimertinib, looking at real-world rebiopsy practice and how second-line therapies performed. Resistance is inevitable; the question is what to do next. The data guide the post-osimertinib decision.
pmc-13217261: In this 2026 genetics paper, recurrent copy number variants — repeated deletions or duplications — were linked to psychiatric outcomes in the context of polygenic scores. Rare big variants and common small ones combine to shape risk. The study integrates both into prediction.
pmc-13424261: This 2026 cross-sectional analysis examined falls in Huntington's disease — clinical features and potential contributors. Falling is a major Huntington's hazard. The analysis identifies the risk factors.
pmc-13424361: In this 2026 bone biology paper, DMP1-Cre expressing cells mediated the gain in bone mass and strength — but not the increased remodeling — induced by parathyroid hormone ligands. The cell population's specific role was dissected. The distinction refines osteoporosis therapy.
pmc-13428261: A 2026 dermatology trial comparing Q-switched versus picosecond 1064-nm laser for tattoo removal — comparable overall effectiveness, with higher excellent clearance rates for one (the title is truncated). The head-to-head test guides laser choice. The trial is the evidence.
pmc-13523761: This 2026 review, "Lighting Up Biology," covered GFP-inspired fluorescent probes for sensing and imaging. The jellyfish protein's legacy continues. The review surveys the probe designs.
pmc-13516261: A 2026 controlled cohort study on adjuvant nonavalent HPV vaccination after LLETZ in patients with isolated CIN2. The vaccine's post-procedure role was tested. The cohort data guide practice.
pmc-13507861: In this 2026 immunology paper, synergistic interaction between macrophage-polarizing signals IL-4 and IFNγ was controlled by the STAT6/STAT1/IRF1 axis. The opposing signals cooperated through the axis. The control mechanism is the finding.
pmc-13494361: In this 2026 mouse study, sciatic denervation differentially remodeled skeletal muscle and deep fascia in the lower limb. Nerve loss changed muscle and fascia differently. The differential remodeling is the finding.
pmc-13487361: In this 2026 mouse study, caffeic acid intervention slowed cancer cell growth while reversing Th2-biased immune balance in colorectal cancer-bearing mice. The coffee compound fought tumors and rebalanced immunity. The dual effect is the finding.
pmc-13598561: A 2026 Chinese-language paper constructing a comprehensive evaluation index system for preconception health care behaviors among people of childbearing age, with empirical research. The index system guides maternal health programs. The construction is the method.
pmc-13402861: A 2026 oncology paper on overcoming radiation resistance — ferroptosis induction to sensitize solid tumors to radiation therapy. The iron-dependent cell death broke resistance. The sensitization is the strategy.
pmc-13402761: A 2026 cross-sectional interaction-mediation analysis of determinants of stress and obstacles to diabetes-related quality of life in adults with type 2 diabetes (the title is truncated). The stress-quality pathways were modeled. The determinants guide support.
pmc-13542661: In this 2026 Nigerian cross-sectional study, clinical significance of lipoprotein and ceruloplasmin variations in type 2 diabetes was examined in Owo. The biomarkers' diabetes role was tested. The variations are the finding.
pmc-13479561: A 2026 Ethiopian cross-sectional study of moral distress and associated factors among nurses in public hospitals in West Arsi Zone. The nurses' moral burden was quantified. The factors guide support.
pmc-13474161: This 2026 correction notice amended a paper on factors influencing HPV vaccination intention and uptake among medical students (the title is truncated). Corrections fix the record. This entry preserves the correction.
pmc-13427061: A 2026 mixed-methods systematic review of barriers and facilitators to implementing digital health technologies for remote management of non-communicable diseases in rural areas. The implementation obstacles were synthesized. The review guides rollout.
pmc-13526461: A 2026 case report of pathologic complete response following frailty-adjusted neoadjuvant paclitaxel in an 88-year-old with radiation-associated breast angiosarcoma. The tailored chemo cured the elderly patient. The response is the hope.
pmc-13437261: In this 2026 single-center study, clinical characteristics and risk factors of pediatric macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia from 2023 to 2025 were analyzed (the title is truncated). The resistant pneumonia's profile was mapped. The analysis informs pediatrics.
pmc-13427761: This 2026 real-world evaluation tested a transformer-based natural language processing system for identifying social determinants of health from routine clinical documentation (the title is truncated). The AI read the social context. The evaluation is the implementation evidence.
pmc-13423161: In this 2026 trial, transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation's effect on postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction was tested following laparoscopic urological surgery (the title is truncated). The electrical stimulation aided gut recovery. The effect is the evidence.
pmc-13421761: A 2026 power systems paper on expert-guided optimization for load transfer in distribution networks assisted by virtual power plants. The grid's load was optimized. The optimizing serves the energy transition.
pmc-13417661: This 2026 Japanese retrospective observational study examined clinical and psychological effects of the JADEC Diabetes Card System using the Problem Areas in Diabetes scale (the title is truncated). The diabetes card's effects were measured. The effects inform diabetes education.
